text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOMMERSANT DAILY
- Russian officials are indignant with European Commission for withholding information about illegal exports of banned British beef, says the paper.
- A presidential decree on gold exports is ready but no details are known yet, says the paper.
- The central bank of Russia has started fixing everyday quotes for gold, silver and platinum.
- The staff of Russia's Defence Ministry will be halved according to a new presidential decree, the details of which are not available so far.
- Russia's prestige as a space superpower will be probably saved by a U.S. austrataut.
- A former Russian diplomat, Platon Obukhov, accused of spying for Britain, will be treated in a mental hospital.
SEVODNYA
- Russia's Perm region plans to issue $150-$200 million in Eurobonds in December or January via Morgan Stanley.
- President Boris Yeltsin signed a decree ordering to set up a commission to protect investor rights and a national depositary.
- Russia is planning to buy about 1.1 million tonnes of Ukrainian sugar by the end of the year.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA
- Nuclear power plant workers who are protesting against wage arrears are not planning to unite with ultra-left movements who are also marching through the capital, says the paper.

- Ingushetia regional president Ruslan Aushev claims a share in the oil transportation deal, under which the pipeline taking Azeri oil to the Russian oil export outlet at Novorossiisk, will cover about 18 km of the territory of Ingushetia.
- The windows of Versace'stores in Moscow are edged with black in a mark of respect for fashion king Gianni Versace, who was brutally murdered on Tuesday.
IZVESTIA
- Russian alcohol market remains largely in the hands of shadowy dealers in spite of all the latest regulatory measures by the government and the president.
- Russia can neither do without beef imports nor control where the meat comes from.
- Russians, who still have to use old Soviet passports to prove their identity, will start receiving new Russian Federation passports from October 1.
- The concept of army reform has been prepared and is likely to be discussed at the next meeting of the Defence Council.
- An aide to ultra-nationalist leader Vladimir Zhirinovsky has been murdered in Moscow. He became the fifth assistant in the controversial politician's party to be killed this year.
- A Spanish company has won the tender to design a high-speed railway link between Moscow and St Petersburg.
- The West will not be able to ignore Slobodan Milosevic after his victory in the presidential election in Yugoslavia.
- A simmering row over a uranium deal between Russia and the U.S. is starting to flare again.
ROSSIISKAYA GAZETA
- The share of the shadow economy in Russia has fallen sharply, says Tax Service head Alexander Pochinok.
- Parliamentary experts have started work on the draft tax code to prepare it for a second reading in the Duma on November 11.
- Japanese automaker Toyota is studying a project to assemble Hi-Ace minibuses in Russia.
MOSKOVSKY KOMSOMOLETS
- Moscow's Sheremetyevo-2 international airport will open its second all-purpose runway on Friday.
- The Russian armed forces, plagued by massive draft dodging, stand at 85 percent of their full peacetime strength after a rather successful spring draft.
--Tatyana Ustinova, Moscow Newsroom, +70941 8520.
